Strip manifest for minimal cosmo/APE C-only toolchain
Source: ~/Projects/work/cosmopolitan/.cosmocc/4.0.2 (Cosmopolitan cosmocc release, GCC 14.1.0)

This is a historical record of what was stripped/kept and why. build/ is
now re-derived from scratch by scripts/stage-toolchain.sh (chained with a
full build+test by scripts/rebuild-from-scratch.sh) rather than by hand --
this file documents the reasoning baked into that script, not a set of
manual steps still left to run.

Current staged layout (build/):
  gcc-amd64/  x86_64-linux-cosmo toolchain, amd64-native binaries, targets amd64
  gcc-arm64/  aarch64-linux-cosmo toolchain, amd64-native binaries, targets arm64
  apelink/    apelink/fixupobj/pecheck, amd64-native only (2026-09-07: an
              arm64-native copy was also staged originally, then dropped for
              the same reason as gcc-arm64-on-amd64/ below -- Blink already
              runs the amd64-native copy on arm64 hosts), plus the ape-*.elf
              loader stubs. apelink and the ape-x86_64.elf/ape-aarch64.elf
              loader stubs are built from this repo's own local source
              (not the prebuilt cosmocc release) so that every program the
              wrapper compiles gets the current ape-loader-path behavior
              (see SUMMARY.md, "Locally-built apelink + ape loader", for
              why and for the two bugs found and worked around getting
              there). fixupobj/pecheck remain prebuilt.
  blink/      blink-arm64.elf only (runs natively on arm64, emulates amd64 guest
              code -- see below for why no blink-amd64.elf is needed; vendored
              as a prebuilt binary, see vendor/ -- no upstream prebuilt release
              and no aarch64 cross-compiler on this host to build one)
  include/    shared, arch-independent headers, staged once
  gold/       NOTE.md only -- no gold linker exists anywhere in this ecosystem

Truncation of trailing unreferenced data (2026-09-07): every `assimilate`d
executable (gcc/cc1/collect2/as/ld.bfd x2 trees, apelink/fixupobj/pecheck
x2 host arches) was found to still physically contain the OTHER
architecture's ELF slice after assimilation -- `assimilate` patches the
active headers/program-header table to select one slice but does NOT
truncate the other slice's bytes away. Confirmed via `readelf -lW`: file
size vs. (offset+filesize) of the last PT_LOAD/TLS/NOTE segment showed
~50% of every assimilated file was outside any loadable segment (e.g.
cc1: 82.4MB file, only 41.5MB actually mapped at runtime). Also applied
to build/blink/blink-arm64.elf for an unrelated but analogous reason: it
ships unstripped with full DWARF debug sections (.debug_info etc.) and a
.symtab/.strtab, none of which are inside any loadable segment either, so
the same "truncate to end of last loadable segment" trick applies (a
normal `strip` would have been more idiomatic here but no aarch64-capable
strip/objcopy was available on this amd64 host).
Verified safe empirically before applying: built a scratch copy of the
whole toolchain with every one of these files truncated to
(last-segment-offset + last-segment-filesize), ran the full
compile->link->apelink pipeline against it end-to-end, and separately
ran the truncated blink-arm64.elf as an actual emulator -- both produced
correct, working output. Then applied to the real staged files and
re-validated the full build + arm64/Blink-dispatch test suite again.
Total: 208.2MB -> 103.7MB across the 17 affected files (saved 104.6MB).
This was the single largest reduction of the whole size-trimming effort.

CORRECTION (2026-09-07, found while fixing the wrapper's own bootstrap
loader bug -- see SUMMARY.md "Locally-built apelink + ape loader"): the
above "truncate to last loadable segment" measurement is incomplete for
any file that self-extracts via the external-loader mechanism
(cc1/as/ld.bfd, and locally-built apelink/loader binaries). Those files
store their OWN self-extraction payload as raw bytes referenced only by
a `dd if="$o" skip=N count=M | gzip -dc` in their embedded shell script
-- a range readelf's segment table has no idea about, sitting right
after the last real ELF segment. Truncating purely by segment end
silently deleted that payload; every zero-trimmed binary in this
project only worked on a truly cold loader-cache state because
something else (almost always the wrapper's own self-extraction,
sharing the same cache path) happened to populate the cache first.
zero-trim.py now also scans each file's own shell-script header for
these `dd` extraction lines and never truncates below the furthest
`skip+count` found, so the "50%/104.6MB" savings figure above is
slightly optimistic (a few KB per binary now survives the trim that
didn't before) but the technique and validation approach are otherwise
unchanged.

Both gcc-amd64/ and gcc-arm64/ are amd64-native (assimilated from the fat APE
originals via `assimilate -x`), not just gcc-amd64/. There is no arm64-native
GCC staged at all. cosmocc-min's resolve_tooldir() picks the tree by TARGET
architecture only; Blink is invoked whenever the HOST is arm64, regardless of
target, since Blink emulates the compiler's own (amd64) execution, which is
independent of what machine code it emits as output. libcosmo.a/crt.o/etc.
are architecture-specific link-time archives, not executables, so both the
amd64 and arm64 copies are always staged regardless of host, to build the two
slices of a fat output binary.

Per-tree contents, assimilated to amd64-native ELF (not fat APE) so the
wrapper can invoke them directly with no APE loader dependency:
  bin/{x86_64,aarch64}-linux-cosmo-{gcc,as,ld.bfd}
  libexec/gcc/{x86_64,aarch64}-linux-cosmo/14.1.0/{cc1,collect2}
Plain-name aliases (bin/as -> bin/x86_64-linux-cosmo-as, bin/ld.bfd ->
bin/x86_64-linux-cosmo-ld.bfd) exist on disk during staging/build, but are
NOT embedded into the final binary (see below); cosmocc-min recreates them
at runtime instead.

Removed 2026-09-07 (unused by cosmocc-min's pipeline): bin/{x86_64,aarch64}-
linux-cosmo-{ar,ranlib,nm,objcopy,objdump,strip,addr2line,size,readelf,
elfedit,ld}. Verified by grepping wrapper/cosmocc-min.c: it only ever execs
the *-gcc driver directly (which internally finds cc1/collect2/as/ld.bfd via
-B), plus the host-side fixupobj/apelink/pecheck. None of ar/nm/ranlib/etc.
are invoked anywhere in the pipeline -- ar/ranlib are only needed to CREATE
static archives (this pipeline only ever produces executables), and ld
reads .a archives' symbol index natively without shelling out to ar/nm.
Plain "ld" (as opposed to ld.bfd) is unused because the wrapper always
passes -fuse-ld=bfd. Verified empirically: built a trimmed copy of the
toolchain missing all of these and ran the full compile+link+apelink
pipeline against it end-to-end -- output was byte-identical to a build
against the untrimmed toolchain. This was the largest remaining reduction
after the two-tree consolidation: it removed roughly two thirds of the
non-cc1/non-libcosmo.a file count per tree.
Note: readelf and elfedit happened to be byte-identical between the
x86_64-linux-cosmo and aarch64-linux-cosmo builds (unlike ar/nm/objcopy/
objdump/strip/addr2line/size, which differ in size despite being logically
architecture-agnostic tools -- confirmed ar and nm still work correctly on
the *other* architecture's object files even though the binaries differ
byte-for-byte, likely due to per-target BFD backend configuration at build
time). Moot now since none of them are staged at all.

Removed entirely, not staged:
  bin/{x86_64,aarch64}-linux-cosmo-{c++,c++filt,g++}   (C++ frontend/driver)
  bin/{x86_64,aarch64}-linux-cosmo-{cc,cpp}             (2026-09-07: unused --
    cosmocc-min only ever invokes the *-gcc driver directly; cc1 has an
    integrated preprocessor for normal -c compiles, so the standalone cpp
    binary is never exec'd, and cc/gcc are the same C driver under different
    argv[0] names. cc/cpp/gcc were byte-identical copies in the upstream
    distribution -- not symlinks -- so removing cc+cpp also removed 2 of the
    3 duplicate copies per tree.)
  libexec/gcc/.../14.1.0/cc1plus                        (C++ compiler proper)
  lib/libstdc++.a, lib/libcxx.a                         (C++ standard libs,
                                                          incl. optlinux/tiny/dbg variants)
  lib/libgomp.a, lib/libgomp.spec                       (GCC OpenMP runtime)
  lib/{dbg,optlinux,tiny}/*                             (2026-09-07: alternate
    cosmo runtime builds for -mdbg/-moptlinux/-mtiny; cosmocc-min never passes
    those flags or references these paths. dbg/libcosmo.a alone was
    ~120-130MB per arch, unstripped. Removing all three variants roughly
    halved each staged toolchain tree.)
  bin/apelink -> not staged directly; only its assimilated apelink-amd64
    copy is (see apelink/ above)
  build/blink/blink-amd64.elf                           (2026-09-07: Blink
    only ever emulates amd64 guest code and is only ever invoked when the
    HOST is arm64 -- a blink-amd64.elf would never be exercised by any code
    path in cosmocc-min, so it was never staged)
  gcc-arm64-on-amd64/ as a SEPARATE tree from gcc-arm64/ (2026-09-07: this
    plan originally staged an arm64-native gcc-arm64/ for arm64 hosts AND a
    separate amd64-native gcc-arm64-on-amd64/ for amd64 hosts. Realized the
    arm64-native copy was unnecessary once Blink is willing to run either
    toolchain on an arm64 host -- kept only the amd64-native tree, renamed to
    gcc-arm64/. This was the single largest size reduction: ~206MB removed.)

Symlink handling (2026-09-07): the plain-name tool aliases (ld, ld.bfd, as,
ar, nm, objcopy, objdump, ranlib, readelf, size, strip, addr2line, elfedit)
created during staging are real filesystem symlinks on disk, but
scripts/embed-assets.py skips them when building the embedded zip payload
(Python's zipfile.write() follows symlinks and would otherwise store a full
duplicate copy of the target's content under the alias name -- this was
costing ~82MB compressed, ~27% of the whole embedded payload, before the
fix). cosmocc-min's create_tool_aliases() recreates these symlinks itself
after extracting the embedded assets at runtime.

Not present in this cosmocc build at all (nothing to remove):
  liblto_plugin*, lto1, libasan*, libtsan*, libubsan* (GCC's own sanitizer
  runtimes) -- this cosmocc release doesn't ship GCC LTO or GCC sanitizer
  support. Cosmopolitan's own libc-level sanitizer support (kept) lives in
  libc.a/libcosmo.a, not as separate GCC runtime libs.

Kept as-is (no C++/LTO/OpenMP content, needed for C compile+link+APE):
  lib/crt.o, lib/libc.a, lib/libcosmo.a, lib/libm.a, lib/libdl.a,
  lib/libpthread.a, lib/librt.a, lib/libcrypt.a, lib/libresolv.a,
  lib/libgcc_s.a, lib/libunwind.a (C-level backtrace/unwind support used by
  ShowCrashReports, not a C++ exception runtime), lib/ape.lds (amd64) /
  lib/aarch64.lds (arm64), lib/ape.o, lib/ape-no-modify-self.o
  include/ (shared, arch-independent headers, copied once, not duplicated
  per arch)

Linker note:
  No cosmo-patched gold (ld.gold) exists anywhere in the Cosmopolitan
  project or the cosmocc release -- verified by grepping the monorepo and
  inspecting the cosmocc bin/ directory. Cosmopolitan itself is built with
  ld.bfd. Per decision, `ld.bfd` (staged per-tree above) substitutes for
  gold throughout this toolchain; see build/gold/NOTE.md.

History note: an earlier iteration of this plan produced two binaries,
blink-compile.com (Binary A, fat outputs) and blink-embed.com (Binary B,
amd64-only outputs + embedded Blink). Binary B was dropped entirely
(2026-09-07) after finding its arm64 auto-relaunch-via-embedded-Blink
mechanism would require either risky in-place binary patching of apelink's
generated shell-script polyglot header, or sacrificing Windows/wine
compatibility. Only blink-compile.com remains.
